name: Sparus Holdings (Southern Cross, The Spear Group, OneVision Utility Services, Allegiant Utility Services, TruCheck)
hq: Norcross / Atlanta area, GA (Southern Cross, per job postings; not verified); Allegiant: Manor, TX; TruCheck: Somerset, KY
ownership: PE-backed: Ridgemont Equity Partners since Mar 2021 (previously Source Capital); Allegiant and TruCheck add-ons Feb 2023
services: Gas leak survey and detection, pipeline inspection and integrity, stray-voltage inspection, utility locating, meter reading/installation/testing, AMI/smart-grid deployment, wood pole inspection (Allegiant). Serves gas, electric and water utilities.
customers: Gas, electric and water utilities; none named in sources
size_hint: Southern Cross alone: 900+ field employees, founded 1946 (Energy Jobs Network profile, weak source); group revenue unknown
recurring_evidence: Federal rules require leak surveys at fixed intervals (49 CFR 192.723). Meter testing and renewal programs recur. AMI deployments are project-based.
red_flags: Would be a secondary buyout after 5+ years of Ridgemont ownership, at sponsor pricing. Labor-intensive, so margins depend on wages. AMI is eroding meter reading. Vehicle-mounted methane sensing is changing leak-survey economics. AMI rollout revenue is lumpy. Website is a subsidiary's (Southern Cross).

name: Heath Consultants
ownership: Private, founded 1933; no PE sponsor found; ownership details not verified
services: Manufactures methane leak-detection instruments and provides gas leak survey services. Sold its gas locating unit to USIC in June 2025.
customers: Decatur Utilities (AL), annual leak survey; other LDC customers not named
size_hint: Unknown; smaller after the 2025 divestiture of gas locating
recurring_evidence: Annual leak-survey contract with Decatur Utilities; federally mandated survey intervals; recurring instrument replacement and service
red_flags: The divestiture suggests pruning or a need for capital. Ownership and succession are unverified. The only named customer is a small municipal utility.

name: Danella Companies
services: Plastic and steel gas mains, metering and regulator stations, gas maintenance and repair; also electric and telecom utility services (background)
recurring_evidence: Ongoing PGW excavation work under city utility permits; offers maintenance and repair
red_flags: 6 OSHA investigations since 2017 over trench work, and on site at a Philadelphia gas-main rupture: fails the 'strong safety record' screen pending diligence. PGW is city-owned, so its work is likely publicly bid.

name: Artera Services (Miller Pipeline, Minnesota Limited, KS Energy Services, Southeast Connections, Hydro-X, Volt Power)
ownership: PE-backed: Clayton, Dubilier & Rice since 2018 (formerly PowerTeam Services)
services: Gas distribution maintenance, repair, modernization and construction; transmission pipeline; hydro-excavation; some electric work (Volt Power)
customers: CenterPoint Energy / Vectren (former parent of Miller Pipeline and Minnesota Limited); other LDCs not named
size_hint: Paid $850M for MVerge (Miller Pipeline + Minnesota Limited) in 2020; total revenue unknown
recurring_evidence: Says utility customers rely on it to maintain, repair and modernize infrastructure; LDC pipe-replacement programs
red_flags: Too large for a FAM entry platform; a CD&R exit would be priced at a sponsor multiple; integration risk of a sponsor-built roll-up; much of the work is replacement capex, not pure maintenance

name: Michels Corporation (incl. Michels Utility Services, Michels Trenchless, power T&D)
services: Diversified infrastructure contractor. Gas: builds, upgrades, repairs and maintains transmission and distribution (cast-iron and bare-steel replacement, risers, meters, relights, regulator stations). Also power T&D, pipeline, tunneling, and trenchless water/sewer rehab.
size_hint: Very large multi-segment contractor (multi-billion per a background estimate; not quantified in sources)
recurring_evidence: Cast-iron and bare-steel replacement programs and gas maintenance services; mostly construction
red_flags: Construction-heavy, not a maintenance pure play; too large for an entry platform; family unlikely to sell. Appeared in the gas, T&D and water lists (merged here).

name: USIC
ownership: PE-backed (current sponsor and entry date not verified)
services: Utility locating and damage prevention; acquired Heath's gas locating business (2025) and Damage Prevention Specialists
size_hint: Largest US locating company (background); not quantified
recurring_evidence: Multi-year locating contracts driven by state one-call laws
red_flags: Too large; volume follows excavation activity rather than asset maintenance; price pressure on per-ticket pricing

name: Q3 Contracting, Inc.
services: Gas distribution construction, joint trench, station construction, system maintenance
recurring_evidence: Lists system maintenance and station work
red_flags: Ownership, size and contract type unverified; construction mix

name: J. F. Kiely Construction Co.
hq: Long Island City, NY (background; not verified)
services: New and replacement gas transmission and distribution mains and services; meter, hydrant and valve replacement; M&R station design-build; cathodic protection; lead service line replacement (gas plus water)
recurring_evidence: Replacement programs, M&R stations and cathodic protection are recurring categories
red_flags: Size and ownership unverified; NYC union labor costs; replacement work depends on utility capex programs

name: Teichert Pipelines (division of A. Teichert & Son)
services: Plastic and copper gas service repair and replacement; customer meter-set repair and replacement; high-pressure regulator upgrades; cathodic protection
size_hint: Unknown (division of a large construction and aggregates group)
recurring_evidence: Repair and replacement plus cathodic protection services
red_flags: Buyable only as a carve-out; California labor costs; website is the parent's

name: Grace Industries LLC
hq: New York City area (background; not verified)
services: Heavy civil and underground utility work (DCA member)
recurring_evidence: Not established
red_flags: Heavy civil contractor probably reliant on low-bid public work, an avoid criterion (inferred from background, not verified)

name: Pro-Vac (incl. Hydromax USA)
hq: Washington state for Pro-Vac (background; not verified); Hydromax USA HQ sources conflict (Omaha, NE / Coppell or Flower Mound, TX / Evansville, IN)
ownership: PE-backed: Gallant Capital Partners. Hydromax USA was owned by Industrial Growth Partners from Dec 2020 (bought from Warren Equity) before Pro-Vac acquired it. The merge is inferred from the title of Pro-Vac's release; confirm.
services: Hydro-excavation and vacuum services; sewer cross-bore inspection for gas-safety programs; gas leak detection; water/wastewater condition assessment; infrastructure mapping and data services
recurring_evidence: Outsourced multi-year cross-bore and inspection programs for utilities
red_flags: Already PE-owned (two sponsor hops for Hydromax); each utility's cross-bore program eventually ends; hydrovac pricing is competitive; sponsor is actively building

name: GPT Industries (incl. Integrated Rectifier Technologies)
ownership: PE-backed: Branford Castle Partners (Fund II platform; entry date not verified)
services: Manufactures pipeline isolation and sealing products and cathodic-protection rectifiers
recurring_evidence: Consumables and replacement parts for cathodic-protection systems
red_flags: A manufacturer, not a services company, so relevant only to the thesis's selective-manufacturing angle. Already PE-owned. Midstream/industrial tilt.

name: T.D. Williamson
services: Hot tapping and plugging, pigging and in-line inspection, pipeline repair; also manufactures the equipment
recurring_evidence: Integrity and maintenance services for pipeline operators
red_flags: Global and focused on midstream/transmission rather than US utility distribution; too large; sourcing is background only

name: ULC Technologies
services: Robotics and technology for gas mains (e.g., the CISBOT cast-iron joint-sealing robot) plus utility field services
recurring_evidence: Not established
red_flags: Revenue is technology/project work rather than recurring maintenance; sourcing is background only

name: Pike Corporation
ownership: PE-backed: TPG Rise Climate + La Caisse majority with management (closed Dec 2025); Lindsay Goldberg 2020-2025; Pike family historically
services: Distribution and transmission construction and maintenance, storm restoration, engineering, renewables/DER, telecom
customers: 400+ investor-owned, municipal and cooperative utilities (unnamed in release)
size_hint: ~12,000 employees (company release, Dec 2025); valuation reported >$5B (Octus via BusinessNC)
recurring_evidence: Long-standing relationships with 400+ utilities; storm and distribution maintenance work for IOUs and co-ops
red_flags: Just recapitalized, so not actionable. Mix includes construction and renewables, not pure maintenance. Direct competitor for T&D add-ons.

name: Osmose Utilities Services
ownership: Infrastructure fund: EQT Infrastructure, acquired from Kohlberg Investors VII (entry date not captured)
services: Wood pole inspection, treatment and restoration; steel structure inspection and rehabilitation; structural engineering
customers: US and Canadian utilities and telecoms (not named)
size_hint: The Canadian unit (PPSI) alone evaluates or treats 250,000+ poles per year
recurring_evidence: Utilities run pole inspection and treatment as multi-year cyclical programs
red_flags: Owned by an infrastructure fund, so not actionable as a platform. Dominant in pole inspection, so it competes for pole add-ons.

name: Asplundh Tree Expert
services: Utility vegetation management / line clearance (~70% of revenue), plus affiliates doing utility line construction and maintenance
customers: Electric utilities nationwide (not named in sources)
size_hint: $4.7B revenue in 2021 (Wikipedia mirror, weak); other estimates of $5.7B-$7.4B unverified
recurring_evidence: Line clearance runs as recurring multi-year utility programs
red_flags: Not for sale; dominant competitor; labor-intensive vegetation work with thin margins and periodic competitive re-bids

name: Davey Tree Expert Co.
ownership: Employee-owned (not exchange-listed; publishes an annual report)
services: Utility line clearance and vegetation management, utility consulting and inspection (Davey Resource Group), plus residential and commercial tree care
recurring_evidence: Multi-year utility vegetation management programs
red_flags: Not for sale. Company-wide 2025 net margin of ~1.7% shows thin economics. $34.5M insurance charge in 2025. Includes a residential/commercial mix.

name: Novinium
ownership: Strategic: Southwire Company (private wire and cable maker), acquired Apr 2022; formerly VC-backed (SJF Ventures)
services: Underground cable rejuvenation (incl. CableCURE, acquired with UtilX) and cable diagnostics/TDR testing
recurring_evidence: Programmatic utility cable rejuvenation programs
red_flags: Owned by Southwire, so not actionable. Proprietary/patented process. Size data is from 2015.

name: Lewis Tree Service
ownership: Privately held; formerly PE-backed per PitchBook; current owner not verified
services: Utility vegetation management / line clearance
recurring_evidence: Line clearance is typically run as multi-year programs (sector norm, not company-specific evidence)

name: Wright Tree Service
services: Utility line clearance and vegetation management
recurring_evidence: Line clearance programs (sector norm; not verified for this company)

recurring_evidence: Line clearance can recur; not evidenced

name: Divergent Alliance
services: Storm response and emergency restoration, supply and services
recurring_evidence: None found

name: OneSource Restoration LLC
services: Deploys damage assessors, linemen and distribution line crews to utilities nationwide for storms
recurring_evidence: None found

name: RS Electric Utility Services
services: Transmission and distribution line work, storm restoration
recurring_evidence: None found

name: Day & Zimmermann
services: Nuclear and fossil (gas/coal) plant maintenance, scheduled and emergency outages, boiler maintenance and repair, modifications. Also has non-power businesses (background).

size_hint: ~46,000 workforce company-wide (company figure; a 2013 release said 23,000, so inconsistent)
recurring_evidence: 5-year We Energies and PSEG Nuclear contracts; 50+ FENOC refueling outages; fleet-wide multi-year nuclear maintenance contract
red_flags: Not for sale; the dominant incumbent and benchmark. Contract examples date from 2012-13. Coal retirements shrink the fossil base. Diversified beyond power.

name: Shermco Industries
services: NETA electrical testing and maintenance, rotating apparatus repair, power systems engineering, training; substation testing
recurring_evidence: Maintenance testing programs; serial NETA add-ons (Power Test, 2024)
red_flags: Just sold to Blackstone, so not actionable. End markets lean commercial/industrial/data center rather than utility. A consolidator competing for NETA add-ons.

name: RESA Power
ownership: PE-backed: Kohlberg & Company (Apr 2025); previously Investcorp (2021) and Blue Sea Capital
services: NETA electrical testing, transformer services, engineering studies, custom/retrofit switchgear and breakers, obsolete-parts inventory
size_hint: 20+ locations in the US and Canada
recurring_evidence: Testing plus parts and service for its installed base across 6,000+ customers
red_flags: On its third sponsor owner, so not actionable; partly a products/parts business

name: Allied Power Group
ownership: PE-backed: Warren Equity Partners per Baird deal card; earlier AEA Investors SBF / Audax (2019). Sources conflict.
services: Aftermarket maintenance and repair of heavy-frame industrial gas turbines, component repair, field services
recurring_evidence: Repeat component repair on outage cycles for utility gas-turbine fleets
red_flags: Sponsor-owned and actively consolidating (TRS Services Aug 2026, Viking Turbine Services Oct 2026): a competitor for add-ons, not actionable

services: Turnkey steam turbine outages for fossil and nuclear units of 1-1,300 MW, gas turbine services, field balancing, machining, borescope inspection, emergency turbine support
size_hint: Unknown; a roll-up of 5 predecessor firms
recurring_evidence: Turbine work on outage cycles across all major OEM fleets
red_flags: Already a roll-up; current ownership unverified; outage revenue is lumpy and seasonal; turnkey outages may carry fixed-price risk

recurring_evidence: Not verified
